notes: ACCESS: Akamai Bot Manager JS interstitial solved with the proven Inditex recipe - copied pipeline/final_list_batch_sn21-30/inditex_interstitial_solver.py's logic into the scratchpad unchanged as w90_solver.py (read-only source untouched), curl_cffi impersonate=chrome with Accept-Language en-GB, POST of the inline-JS proof-of-work answer plus the page bm-verify token to /_sec/verify?provider=interstitial. Cookies then reused for every itxrest call and every PLP fetch; no proxy needed. STORE: GB storefront store 84009906 / catalog 80290024 (a genuinely separate Inditex catalogue from S.N. 21 Zara Home UAE's 85009931/50333562, per the prior Home-Decor pass which proved differing per-country product populations on the shared taxonomy IDs). TREE: full category tree from /itxrest/2/catalog/store/84009906/80290024/category?languageId=-1&appId=1 (1.16 MB, 706 nodes walked). Zara Home GB has ONE furniture department, node 1020564154 FURNITURE (/gb/furniture-all-n4143), and it is FLAT - none of its children has subcategories, so every child is a leaf and there are no grouping rows to emit. Each node's attachments carry HIDE_CATEGORY_MENU, which distinguishes menu-visible from hidden nodes; 'Console tables' (1020448936) is hidden but live and is kept. QTY METHOD: Zara Home publishes no 'N items' / 'Showing 1-N of M' header anywhere on the site and numberOfProducts is null for every node in the category tree, so qty is the exact size of the node's own server-rendered grid - the unique ccIds returned by /itxrest/3/catalog/store/84009906/80290024/category/<id>/product. VALIDATION: for all 21 emitted leaves I also fetched the canonical SEO PLP and parsed the page's OWN embedded transfer-state entry for /itxrest/3/.../category/<id>/product?showProducts=false&showNoStock=false&withSubCategories=false&languageId=-1; the rendered category id matched the intended node and the rendered ccId count matched the API count in 21 of 21 cases. Top-level productIds equalled unique ccIds on every node. Colour-filter cross-check on 4 control nodes: the union of colFilter productIds equalled the grid exactly on Couches (38), Stools (28) and Side Tables (25), and was 43 of 44 on Kids Furniture (one item has no colour group) - confirming the grid payload is the node's whole catalogue, not a first page. Every count was read twice with the cache cleared between reads: 0 drift on 21 of 21. Counts range 2-44, none equals the department total (285) and none is a round display cap. Every PLP <title> was checked against the node name (e.g. furniture-cabinets-n4899 -> 'Sideboards and Cabinets', bathroom-furniture-n2469 -> 'Bathroom Furniture'); no slug silently served a parent listing. EXCLUDED per brief section 3: SEE ALL (furniture-n4104, 285 items), BESTSELLERS (same slug), the VINCENT VAN DUYSEN designer collection (vincent-van-duysen-furniture-n3879, 29 items - its slug renders no grid payload at all), and the seasonal BACK TO SCHOOL > 'Desks and chairs' node (whose slug is just kids-furniture-n1122 again). DUPLICATE ROLLUPS DROPPED (product-ID overlap measured against the union of the 21 emitted leaves, 292 distinct products): KITCHEN FURNITURE (kitchen-furniture-n1409, 18 items, 18/18 already inside Stools + Storage Furniture + Bathroom Furniture + Sideboards + Shelving - a pure duplicate, exactly as the S.N. 21 UAE worker found); MUEBLES COMEDOR / Dining room furniture (dining-furniture-all-n4740, 18 items, 16/18 inside Chairs + Dining Tables + Outdoor, the 2 others being 'TABLE 01' and 'TABLE 03'); OFFICE (furniture-office-n5761, 20 items, 17/20 inside Desks + Shelving Units + Sideboards + Chairs, the 3 others being 'DESK 01' x2 and 'DESK 02'); BEDROOM FURNITURE (bedroom-furniture-all-n4130, 30 items, 29/30 inside Bedside Tables + Side Tables + Headboards + Bed Frames + Sideboards + Storage + Coat Stands + Console Tables + Kids + Stools, the single other being one ash chest of drawers). This is the one deliberate divergence from the S.N. 21 UAE result, which kept Bedroom Furniture: on the AE store that node carried bedroom-only types with no leaf of their own, whereas the GB store publishes explicit Headboards, Bed Frames and Bedside Tables leaves, so keeping it here would have double-counted 29 of its 30 products. ALSO CHECKED AND DROPPED: BEDDING > DRESSING ROOM AND HANGERS > 'Furniture' (8 items - clothes rails, dressing table, valet stand, stool, luggage rack, shoe bench - all 8 already inside the emitted leaves, and its slug is just furniture-n4104 anyway); BEDDING > 'BEDS AND HEADBOARDS' and KIDS AND BABY > 'FURNITURE', both of which resolve to slugs already emitted (bedroom-bed-frames-n4166 and kids-furniture-n1122) - the rendered pages serve categories 1020567657 (4) and 1020576160 (44), which are the rows emitted, so no duplicate-link rows were created; KIDS AND BABY > BABY > 'Cot and rest beds' (baby-bed-linen-n3948, 41 items) - dropped because the grid is predominantly baby textiles (blankets, cot bumper covers, sheet sets, changing-mat covers, mattresses) with only ~8 actual cots, so its primary product type is bedding, not furniture, and the cots themselves are already inside Kids Furniture; PETS COLLECTION > BEDS (pet beds, not furniture). OUT OF SCOPE, left behind: the FURNITURE department's own MIRRORS entry (renders the Home Decor mirrors landing) and all other mirrors, lamps and lighting, rugs, cushions, throws, curtains, bed linen, duvets, pillows, toppers, mattress protectors, towels, bath mats, bathrobes, bathroom accessories and fixtures, laundry baskets, baskets and boxes, tableware, glassware, cutlery, cookware, table linen, vases, flowerpots, candles, candle holders, photo frames, door knobs and hooks, fragrances, toys, stationery, clothing and footwear. OUTDOOR: unlike the AE store, the GB store does have an outdoor furniture node (furniture-outdoor-n4250) and it is emitted.
